body: uhm, why is this copying the buffers? Sure, they are probably tiny for sprites, but this still looks unnecessary. I am fairly certain that `Vector` overrides the `=` operator, so is there anything stopping us from just using that and avoiding the memcopy?
nitpick, but couldn't this be `pragma pack(push, 1)`?

This avoids an unnecessary memory deallocation + reallocation.

Vectors are reference-counted and copy-on-write, so by using =, the old vector's reference count would become 0 and get released, and the new vector will get written to right after `_stop_sharing_sprite()`, causing a new copy to be reallocated.
That's a good point. I'm seeing `#pragma pack(push, 1)` used elsewhere in the engine too, so I'll be going with the preestablished usage.

any reason why you start a new loop for this? imo you could combine this with the loop above by branching based on whether successor == null.

If you have any scenario where the first 99% of users have switched sprite the current code would iterate over all of them twice, even though the same could be accomplished with just half the iterations.

Not quite. Notice how it's not `for (int i = 0; i < users.size(); i++)` but rather `for (; i < users.size(); i++)`. The loop starts where the last loop is left off, and the total number of iterations is still `users.size()`. By splitting the for loop into two, unnecessary branching is avoided and the code also looks a bit more clean, because this second for loop is exclusively for what comes *after* the successor has been found.
